etymologies.etymologyHTML: From atom +‎ -ic.

definitions.definition: (physics, chemistry) Of or relating to atoms; composed of atoms; monatomic.
Employing or relating to nuclear energy or processes.

quote.citation: 1955, David J. Dallin, Soviet Espionage, page 495:
quote.text: Before the atomic spy Allan Nunn May left Canada to go to London, a treff in London had to be arranged for him and another agent.

definitions.definition: (programming, of a commit in a VCS) Containing a single change, as opposed to involving numerous unrelated changes.
(logic, of a proposition) Lacking logical operators; unable to be made simpler in logical form.

(computing, of an operation) Guaranteed to complete either fully or not at all while waiting in a pause, and running synchronously when called by multiple asynchronous threads.

quote.citation: 2006, Tim Peierls, Brian Goetz, Joshua Bloch, Joseph Bowbeer, Doug Lea, David Holmes, Java Concurrency in Practice, Pearson Education, →ISBN, page 325:
quote.text: It also provides an atomic compareAndSet method (which if successful has the memory effects of both reading and writing a volatile variable) and, for convenience, atomic add, increment, and decrement methods.
